note: Russian, Chinese, Iranian and North Korean navy ships from public reporting (Japan Joint Staff Office, Taiwan MND, Royal Navy, news and OSINT). Positions are approximate, placed in open water near the last reported area; live AIS sightings are added when these ships broadcast, which is rare.

items.name: CNS Liaoning (16)
items.area: Philippine Sea, beyond the first island chain
items.note: Leading a PLA Navy task group on training in the Western Pacific since late October; Taiwan's defense minister said on Nov 10 the group practiced area-denial operations.

src.title: Army Recognition — Liaoning carrier group area-denial drills (Nov 2026)

items.name: CNS Fujian (18)
items.note: China's newest carrier, based at Sanya on Hainan; seen at sea in the South China Sea in Nov 2 satellite imagery and expected to reach full readiness by the end of 2026.

src.title: Newsweek — China's carriers active in the Western Pacific

items.name: CNS Anshan (103)
items.area: Pacific, east of the Osumi Strait (Japan)
items.note: Led a three-ship PLA Navy group east through the Osumi Strait into the Pacific on Nov 11, tracked by Japan's Maritime Self-Defense Force.

src.title: Defence Blog — Japan confirms Chinese warships sailing east of Kyushu

items.name: RFS Stoikiy (545)
items.note: Baltic Fleet corvette escorting convoys of Russian cargo ships out of the Baltic through the Danish straits; seen in the Great Belt on Nov 7 (OSINT reporting).

src.title: United24 — Russian corvette escorts cargo convoys through Danish straits

items.name: IRGC Navy fast-attack boats
items.cls: Revolutionary Guard fast attack craft and small boats
items.note: The regular Iranian Navy lost its frigates and corvettes in the 2026 war, but the Revolutionary Guard's small boats were still attacking tankers in the strait in November. Marker shows the area, not individual boats.

items.name: Choe Hyon (51)
items.note: North Korea's largest warship, commissioned June 23, 2026 into the West Sea Fleet to defend the western coast. A sister ship, Kang Kon, followed in September. Exact position not reported.
